name: webapp
description: A framework-free web backend: routing, accounts with password hashing, bearer-token sessions, role permissions and a per-client rate limiter.
author: test-split author (agent, written without reading the reviewer)

issues.description: The limiter promises at most `limit` requests per window, but it only rejects once more than `limit` hits are recorded, so `limit + 1` requests get through.

Using a session is documented to move its expiry to idle_timeout seconds after the call, but the new expiry is computed from created_at, so it never moves and active users are logged out idle_timeout seconds after login.
issues.fix_hint: Set expires_at to now + idle_timeout (max_age is already enforced by _is_expired).

issues.description: The class says a successful login starts the failure count again from zero, but the success path never resets failed_logins, so failures spread over many sessions add up and lock the account.
issues.fix_hint: Set user.failed_logins = 0 when the password verifies.

issues.description: Session tokens are bearer credentials but are drawn from the random module's Mersenne Twister, whose output can be predicted from earlier outputs or a known seed.
issues.fix_hint: Use the secrets module (secrets.token_urlsafe, secrets.choice) or random.SystemRandom.

issues.description: The rule 'a user may manage their own account, others need user:manage' lives in permissions.can_manage_user, but delete_user re-implements it inline in the HTTP layer and checks the ADMIN role instead of the permission, so the two copies will drift when roles change.
Five nested ifs where early returns would keep the function flat and readable.
The minimum password length 10 is a bare literal repeated in register and change_password (and in their messages) instead of one named constant.

decoys.why_it_is_fine: It deletes from the dict while looping over a list copy of its items, which is safe.
The broad except logs the failure with the request line and re-raises it; nothing is swallowed.
